publications.assertionSummary: Section 8.2, 'Why C(ii) does not rise higher: his household stopped because his children were dying, not because he left.'

incoming.explanation: The mortality reading is why the household is not emigrant-shaped.

outgoing.explanation: The household stops for a documented reason, while the head's own absence remains uninterpretable inside the register defect; the two must be read together rather than merged.
The mortality reading is built on the burial roster's five entries of November 1637 to March 1638/9.

shortLabel: C(ii)'s household stopped because his children were dying, not because he left

sources.alignmentNote: Supplies the terminal baptism the departure reading rested on.
sources.locator: The father-John baptism run ending at Francis 1636/7
The five burials of November 1637 to March 1638/9 in the Berkhamsted roster

statement: The younger Berkhamsted John was opened as a candidate on a departure-shaped gap in the record, and that gap does not exist. His household's last baptism is Francis in 1636/7; within the following two years the parish buried Joane (November 1637), Richard (June 1638), William (October 1638), Elizabeth (February 1638/9) and Francis (March 1638/9), and two of those are demonstrably his own children. A household that loses four or five members in eighteen months and then stops appearing in the baptism register is displaying mortality, not departure. The finding matters beyond this candidate: a departure-shaped gap is only evidence where the burial series for the same parish and window has been read and shown to be covered.
